Microfibrillated Cellulose for Formulation Development

Microfibrillated cellulose (MFC) is cellulose with a fine fibrillar structure. In water, interacting fibrils can form a physical network that influences flow, suspension and texture.

Request a Sample ↗

Bio-Based Rheology and Suspension Solutions

Rheology

A fibril network can provide structure at rest and flow more readily under shear. Behaviour depends on concentration, dispersion and the surrounding formulation.

Suspension

Network structure can help resist particle settling. Particle properties, storage conditions and the finished formula determine the result.

Water interaction

MFC is dispersed rather than dissolved in water. Its interaction with water and other ingredients contributes to the behaviour of the overall system.

Buyer questions

What is microfibrillated cellulose?

MFC is a fibrillar form of cellulose. It is distinct from dissolved cellulose derivatives and from particulate microcrystalline cellulose.

What is MFC used for?

MFC is investigated for rheology, particle suspension, texture and material structure. Suitability depends on the particular grade and application.

How is MFC different from conventional cellulose thickeners?

Many conventional cellulose thickeners are soluble derivatives. MFC instead forms a dispersed fibril network; comparisons should consider flow, recovery and suspension, not just a single viscosity value.
